title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1970-02-27
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway

ai_review.summary: High‑fidelity soundboard capture with a standout NFA → Lovelight suite and strong early‑70s performances like Good Lovin' and Easy Wind.
ai_review.review: The recording is widely praised for its crystal‑clear sound (often rated 9/10 or A+), despite occasional vocal/high‑hat quirks. Musically the show shines thanks to an epic Not Fade Away → Lovelight sequence, stellar Phil Lesh bass work, and memorable renditions of Good Lovin', Easy Wind and Dancin'. Overall listeners consider it one of the better Family Dog shows of early 1970.

ai_rating.rationale: Twelve detailed reviews skew heavily positive (average 4‑star rating), highlighting excellent sound quality and several marquee performances; minor recording hiccups do not outweigh the overall excellence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Most reviewers describe the audio as crisp, A+ or ~9/10. A few note slight vocal/high‑hat imbalance and a minor cut on Casey Jones, but no major dropouts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The early‑70 set is solid with a long, flowing Lovelight centerpiece; occasional sloppiness is mentioned but the overall energy and band cohesion are praised.

band_member_comments.Phil: Multiple reviewers call Phil Lesh phenomenal, noting his thumping bass lines and tight harmony work.
